description: Functions, parameters, return values, scope and recursion in C

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to specify that a function does not return any value?
questions.explanation: The void keyword is used as the return type when a function does not return a value.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct function declaration in C?
questions.explanation: A function declaration specifies the return type, function name and parameter types.

questions.questionText: Which part of a function contains the statements that are executed when the function is called?
questions.explanation: The function body contains the statements that execute when the function is called.

questions.questionText: What is the correct way to call a function named add that takes two arguments?
questions.explanation: A function is called by writing its name followed by arguments inside parentheses.

questions.questionText: What are the values passed to a function when it is called known as?
questions.explanation: The actual values passed during a function call are called arguments.

questions.questionText: What are the variables listed in a function definition called?
questions.explanation: Variables specified in the function definition are called formal parameters.

questions.questionText: Which statement is used to send a value back from a function?
questions.explanation: The return statement sends a value back to the calling function.

questions.questionText: What is the return type of the following function? int square(int n)
questions.explanation: The keyword before the function name specifies its return type. Here it is int.

questions.questionText: What will be the output of the following code? int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; } int main() { printf("%d", add(3, 4)); }
questions.explanation: The function returns 3 + 4, which is 7.

questions.questionText: What will happen if a non-void function reaches the end without returning a value?
questions.optionC: It results in undefined behavior if its returned value is used
questions.explanation: Reaching the end of a value-returning function without returning a value leads to undefined behavior when the returned value is used.

questions.questionText: In C, arguments are normally passed to functions by:
questions.explanation: C uses pass-by-value. A copy of the argument's value is passed to the function.

questions.questionText: What happens to a local variable after the function in which it is declared finishes execution?
questions.explanation: An ordinary local automatic variable exists during the execution of its block or function.

questions.questionText: Which variable can be accessed by multiple functions when declared outside all functions?
questions.explanation: A variable declared outside all functions has file scope and can generally be accessed by functions in that file, subject to scope rules.

questions.questionText: What is the scope of a variable declared inside a function?
questions.optionA: The function/block where it is declared
questions.explanation: A local variable declared inside a function or block is accessible within its applicable block scope.

questions.questionText: Which keyword can be used to preserve the value of a local variable between function calls?
questions.explanation: A static local variable retains its value between function calls.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? void test() { static int x = 0; x++; printf("%d ", x); } int main() { test(); test(); test(); }
questions.explanation: The static variable retains its value between calls, so x becomes 1, then 2, then 3.

questions.questionText: Which function is automatically called first when a C program starts execution?
questions.explanation: Program execution begins with the main function.

questions.questionText: A function that calls itself is called a:
questions.explanation: A function that directly or indirectly calls itself is called a recursive function.

questions.questionText: Which is essential in a recursive function to stop further recursive calls?
questions.explanation: A base condition provides the stopping condition for recursion.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int fact(int n) { if(n == 0) return 1; return n * fact(n - 1); } int main() { printf("%d", fact(4)); }
What will be the output? void change(int x) { x = 100; } int main() { int a = 10; change(a); printf("%d", a); }
questions.explanation: C passes the value of a to x. Changing x does not change the original variable a.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a valid function definition?
questions.optionA: add int(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
questions.optionB: int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
questions.optionC: function add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
questions.optionD: define int add(int a, int b);
questions.explanation: A function definition contains the return type, function name, parameters and function body.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of a function prototype?
questions.optionD: To tell the compiler about the function's name, return type and parameters
questions.explanation: A function prototype informs the compiler about a function before its actual definition is encountered.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int square(int n) { return n * n; } int main() { int x = 5; x = square(x); printf("%d", x); }
questions.explanation: square(5) returns 25, and that value is assigned to x.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int fun(int n) { if(n <= 1) return n; return fun(n - 1) + fun(n - 2); } int main() { printf("%d", fun(5)); }
questions.explanation: This is the Fibonacci recurrence. fun(5) = 5 + 3 = 8.
